title: Fitting a door finger plate and kick plate
subtitle: Screw a finger plate above the handle and a kick plate at the base of a door to protect the paintwork in a hallway or commercial space
excerpt: How to fit a finger plate above the door handle and a kick plate at the door base. Covers marking the position, drilling clean pilot holes through the plate and door, and fixing with machine screws.
sourceNotes: Collins Complete DIY Manual (referenced, not reproduced). UK architectural ironmongery trade practice.

glossaryTerms.definition: A vertical protective plate fitted above the door handle on the push side, to protect the door paintwork from hand contact. Usually 75-80 mm wide and 350-500 mm tall. Available in brass, stainless steel, chrome, and painted steel.

A horizontal protective plate fitted across the bottom of a door, usually 150-200 mm tall. Protects the door face from foot scuffs when the door is pushed open with the foot. Fitted on the face side of an outward-opening door, or both sides for a swing door.

content.text: protect a door from the marks that door furniture and everyday use leave on paintwork. Both fix with machine screws through the plate and the door. The job is measure, drill, and fix.

The finger plate is centred on the door width and positioned directly above the handle. Standard position: the bottom edge of the plate sits 50 mm above the top of the handle backplate. Check it sits clear of the latch position. The kick plate runs across the full width of the door leaf or is cut 20 mm shorter on each side to clear the door frame stops. Mark its top edge 180-200 mm above the floor, or to match an existing plate on another door in the building.

Hold the plate in position and mark through the fixing holes onto the door face with a pencil. Remove the plate. Drill pilot holes with a 4 mm wood bit at each marked position; go fully through the door. The machine screws supplied with the plate pass all the way through the door and are secured with barrel nuts on the back face. Check the hole positions are square to the door face before drilling.

Position the plate over the holes. Fit the machine screws from the front, threading the barrel nuts onto the back. Tighten by hand first, check the plate is straight, then tighten fully with a screwdriver. Do not overtighten; the plate should sit flush and firm without pulling into the door face. For the kick plate on a painted door, apply a thin bead of clear silicone around the perimeter of the plate back before fixing; this seals the gap against moisture.

attrs.symptom: The plate rattles slightly after fixing
attrs.cause: Barrel nuts not tightened fully, or the plate is slightly bowed and not sitting flat.
attrs.fix: Tighten the barrel nuts fully. If the plate is bowed, apply a thin packing shim behind the high corners.

attrs.symptom: Machine screws spin and will not tighten
attrs.cause: The barrel nut is not in the correct position (it spins in its hole rather than locking).
attrs.fix: Hold the barrel nut in position with a finger through the back face hole while tightening the machine screw from the front.
